name: hospitality-alt-data-dashboard
what_it_holds: Streamlit research tool building a near-real-time US lodging-demand proxy for MAR/HLT/H between earnings prints, from entirely free/keyless public sources: TSA checkpoint throughput (2019+), Google Trends brand search (pytrends, 6 hotel brands), BLS employment/JOLTS/PPI for traveler accommodation, yfinance prices/earnings dates, plus one committed hand-keyed file `data/reported_revpar.csv` (quarterly RevPAR for MAR/HLT/H with source URLs — same underlying idea as our 'MAR/HLT RevPAR from releases' but committed as a clean CSV with source links). README states explicitly this is a RevPAR *proxy*, not real STR data ("True RevPAR is STR data (paid)"), substituting BLS accommodation employment/PPI as demand/rate proxies. Reports its own honest backtest: deseasonalized MoM r≈0.41 (p≈0.003) vs RevPAR, but a composite TSA+brand-search+JOLTS signal fails out of sample (r=-0.14 steady state, p≈0.09 on a trading overlay). 32 commits, CI runs daily to refresh data and publish outputs as GitHub Actions artifacts; no paid keys required (optional BLS_API_KEY for higher limits).
why_useful: Directly on gap #8 (hotel supply/demand STR/CoStar proxy) and gap #17 (nowcasting method transparency). Even though it is explicitly a proxy rather than licensed STR data, it is a working, keyless, one-command pull architecture (TSA+BLS+PPI+Trends+yfinance) we could fork or mine for the BLS accommodation-employment/PPI series we may not already be pulling, and its self-reported failure of the composite signal is a useful negative data point consistent with our own TSA/Trends null results.
size_hint: small hand-keyed CSV + gitignored cached pulls; 32 commits
last_activity: not confirmed in fetch (active enough to run daily CI as of check)
duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our existing 'MAR/HLT RevPAR from releases' and our own tested-and-failed TSA-throughput / Google-Trends constructions — still worth flagging for the BLS PPI/accommodation-employment proxy angle we may not have tried, and as a second working example of the same null result on TSA/Trends.
themes: Hotel performance data: STR / CoStar weekly and monthly US RevPAR figures scraped from press releases, HotStats, Smith Travel history compiled on GitHub
Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: Directly on gap #8 (hotel supply/demand STR/CoStar proxy) and gap #17 (nowcasting method transparency). Even though it is explicitly a proxy rather than licensed STR data, it is a working, keyless, one-command pull architecture (TSA+BLS+PPI+Trends+yfinance) we could fork or mine for the BLS accommodation-employment/PPI series we may not already be pulling, and its self-reported failure of the composite signal is a useful negative data point consistent with our own TSA/Trends null results.

Directly matches gap #8 (regional RevPAR, hotel demand) with an actual committed multi-year reported-RevPAR CSV plus a live, no-key pipeline (TSA/BLS/Trends/yfinance) for hotel-brand demand proxies that read through to STR competitive pricing pressure.

The PPI Traveler Accommodation series is a monthly hotel-room-rate price index (adjacent to CPI lodging, arguably a cleaner room-rate proxy since it is closer to producer pricing) with an automated pull method; the committed reported-RevPAR CSV (2019-2026) is independently useful for gap #8 (hotel supply/demand RevPAR) as a hand-collected, already-tabulated series saving re-transcription from 10-Qs.

name: jtilly/cbpR
what_it_holds: R package that downloads and assembles panel datasets from the U.S. Census Bureau's County Business Patterns (CBP) program, aggregable to county/metro/micro level; `getFirmCount()`-style functions accept a NAICS code (demonstrated with a 6-digit code, so NAICS 721 'Accommodation' / 721110 'Hotels and Motels' is selectable), and years are user-specified (demo shown for 2000-2009, but CBP itself runs 1986-2023 annual).
why_useful: CBP publishes annual county-level establishment counts, employment and payroll for NAICS 721 (Accommodation and Food Services > Accommodation) — a free, long-run, granular US hotel-supply census (number of hotel establishments, employment) that could be turned into a US hotel-supply-growth series to compare against Airbnb's US listing growth. Directly addresses gap 8 (hotel supply) with public, county-level government data going back further than any commercial STR/CoStar series we hold.
time_coverage: CBP program spans 1986-2023 annually; package demo covers 2000-2009 but is not hardcoded to that range
size_hint: Tooling + cached CBP panel builds, CBP source files are tens of MB/year
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
why_all: CBP publishes annual county-level establishment counts, employment and payroll for NAICS 721 (Accommodation and Food Services > Accommodation) — a free, long-run, granular US hotel-supply census (number of hotel establishments, employment) that could be turned into a US hotel-supply-growth series to compare against Airbnb's US listing growth. Directly addresses gap 8 (hotel supply) with public, county-level government data going back further than any commercial STR/CoStar series we hold.

name: OvertureMaps/overturemaps-py
what_it_holds: Official Overture Maps Foundation Python CLI (MIT license, 266 stars, 270 commits). Downloads Overture data for a bbox/region and a theme (places, buildings, transportation, divisions, base, addresses) and converts to GeoParquet/GeoJSON/etc. Places theme covers global POIs including accommodation/lodging categories (confirmed via schema repo cross-check, exact category list not extracted). Data underneath lives on S3/Azure as versioned monthly releases (STAC catalog), so pulling the same bbox at different Overture release dates gives a point-in-time-ish hotel/lodging POI count by city or metro.
why_useful: This is the practical one-command tool to actually pull the places theme (hotels/lodging category) for named cities/regions and diff across releases — turns the Overture places theme (row above) into something the team can script without hand-rolling Parquet/S3 access.
themes: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
wildcard: a computational social scientist who works with Reddit dumps
why_all: This is the practical one-command tool to actually pull the places theme (hotels/lodging category) for named cities/regions and diff across releases — turns the Overture places theme (row above) into something the team can script without hand-rolling Parquet/S3 access.

Gap #8/#9/#20: a free, global, monthly-versioned alternative to Inside Airbnb/AirDNA for counting STR-adjacent and hotel POIs by city, and for tracking new-supply growth (hotel openings, lodging POI density) as a cross-check on our Inside Airbnb listing counts. Also usable to build regional tourism-POI density controls (restaurants, attractions) as demand proxies.

A source of short-term-rental-adjacent and hotel POI density/counts by city that is independent of Inside Airbnb's own listing scrape, potentially usable as a supply cross-check or for markets outside the current 123-market Inside Airbnb panel (gap #8/#20 geospatial angle); actively maintained, quarterly-versioned open releases.

name: diegoantognini/HotelRec
what_it_holds: ~50 million TripAdvisor hotel reviews (paper claims this is the largest public hotel-review corpus), far larger than the 515k Booking.com Kaggle set we already hold. Each record: hotel URL, author, review DATE, overall rating, title, text, and sub-ratings (sleep quality, value, rooms, service, cleanliness, location). Repo has loader/preprocessing code; actual JSON data is hosted off-GitHub at https://drive.switch.ch/index.php/s/n48smsdufhRA7fR (academic-research-only licence, no commercial redistribution). 73 stars, last updated Jun 2026 (repo maintained), underlying data collected pre-2020 per README sample (earliest sample review 2010; full date range not stated in README).
why_useful: Dated per-hotel reviews at massive scale are the closest open substitute for a review-velocity/occupancy-nowcast panel (gap #2 realised occupancy proxy, and this scout's core theme) — review counts by date and hotel could be aggregated into a review-velocity time series by city/country as a hotel-demand proxy, the same logic as our reviews-based Airbnb 'stays index'. Caveat: appears to be a static historical crawl (not continuously updated), so its usefulness is as a backtest/calibration set for review-velocity-as-demand methodology, not a live feed; and licence is academic-only.
license: unspecified in README; explicit 'academic research purpose only' restriction
time_coverage: reviews dated but full span unclear from README (sample shown from 2010); likely covers ~2002-2019 given TripAdvisor crawl era
last_activity: 2026-06-26 (repo), underlying data crawl likely much older
duplicate_of_holding: extends/supersedes the 515k Booking.com Kaggle hotel-review set we already hold (different source, ~100x larger, but Booking vs TripAdvisor)
themes: Hotel and STR reviews as demand: review velocity datasets (Google, TripAdvisor, Booking) with dates; review-based nowcasting repos
why_all: Dated per-hotel reviews at massive scale are the closest open substitute for a review-velocity/occupancy-nowcast panel (gap #2 realised occupancy proxy, and this scout's core theme) — review counts by date and hotel could be aggregated into a review-velocity time series by city/country as a hotel-demand proxy, the same logic as our reviews-based Airbnb 'stays index'. Caveat: appears to be a static historical crawl (not continuously updated), so its usefulness is as a backtest/calibration set for review-velocity-as-demand methodology, not a live feed; and licence is academic-only.

A large, dated, global TripAdvisor review corpus is exactly the raw material for building a review-velocity/review-count demand index (counts of new reviews per hotel per month as an occupancy/nights proxy), addressing gap #2 (realised occupancy proxy) and gap #17 (nowcasting methods) using a non-Airbnb site. Historical depth (2010+) also lets a velocity-vs-known-RevPAR backtest be built further back than our current sources.

name: Dubai-Tourism-Data-Analysis-

why_useful: Direct-to-KPI: hotel establishment performance (occupancy/ADR proxy), overnight visitors by region/source market, and visitor nationality counts are exactly the kind of MEA travel-demand series named in gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) and could proxy Gulf inbound STR demand feeding ABNB EMEA/APAC splits.
